events.action: User sends first message to girl
events.context: User replies with three points: 1. Explains friend zone and anxiety from her pushing; 2. Clarifies no material expectations, rejects obedience tests; 3. States frustration is normal.
Advisor praises sincerity but points out user focused on own anxiety instead of answering her core question about commitment.
'你有焦虑症？我说的是让你下周前回复。你焦虑什么？' (Do you have anxiety? I said reply before next week. What are you anxious about?)
Recommends admitting anxiety source honestly, e.g., '怕你跑了' (Afraid you'll leave); warns against explaining or flipping old issues.
'你有焦虑症？我说的是让你下周“前”回复啊。你焦虑什么？不要用问题回答别人的问题。' (Don't answer questions with questions.)
Urges direct answer like '我焦虑的是，我怕我做不到' (Anxious I can't do it); presents binary choice: commit or end.
'你怎么昨天今天焦虑发作，平时回避发作？哪个是baseline你定个调。' (Anxiety today, avoidance usually? Pick your baseline.)
Sees it as her handing over definition rights; suggests '焦虑是真的，回避是怕你走' (Anxiety real, avoidance from fear of you leaving).
'你到底焦虑还是回避？' (Are you anxious or avoidant?)
Analyzes user as anxious-avoidant hybrid; suggests admitting '我想靠近你。但我一靠近，就害怕。一害怕，就想跑。'
'你到底焦虑还是回避？I’m not gonna deal with it. I asked questions, you went on about you, you and you.' (Tired of user's self-focus.)
Notes girl wants 'we' focus, not therapy; presents final binary options: explain (dead end) or commit/quit.
